name: Julia Koch
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Julia Koch and her three children inherited a 42% stake in Koch, Inc. (formerly Koch Industries) from her husband, David Koch, who died in 2019 at age 79.
An Iowa native, Koch moved to New York City in the 1980s and worked as an assistant to fashion designer Adolfo.
She worked with many of his high-profile clients, including First Lady Nancy Reagan.
Julia met David via a blind date in 1991; they ran into each other again six months later, began dating and got married in 1996.
In 2024, Koch and her three children paid nearly $700 million for 15% of BSE Global, which owns the NBA's Brooklyn Nets and WNBA's New York Liberty.
In 2025, the family acquired 10% of the NFL's New York Giants in a deal valuing the team at more than $10 billion.
forbes_facts: Julia Koch serves on the boards of Koch, Inc., Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and The Metropolitan Museum of Art.

name: Nicola Forrest
forbes_bio: Forrest founded Fortescue Metals Group in 2003. It's an iron ore giant which is now transforming itself into a green energy powerhouse.
Andrew and his wife Nicola announced their separation in July 2023 - after more than three decades of marriage.
Andrew chairs his Minderoo Foundation. - a philanthropic outfit with an $9 billion (AUD) endowment focussed on everything from gender equality to climate change to rebuilding Ukraine.
In December 2022, his privately held Squadron Energy paid an estimated A$4 billion for Australia's biggest wind energy company, CWP Renewables.
Forrest has also promised to spend A$750 million on rebuilding Ukraine's energy and communications infrastructure.
forbes_facts: Known by his schoolboy nickname "Twiggy," Forrest was a onetime stockbroker and keen amateur boxer.
He once tried to make a living as an alpaca farmer and is a descendant of the first premier of the state of West Australia, Lord Forrest of Bunbury.
Regarded as Australia's biggest philanthropist, he made the country's largest-ever donation in 2019, gifting A$655 million to a variety of causes.

name: Ivan Glasenberg
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Ivan Glasenberg holds the largest individual stake in Glencore, the world's biggest commodity trader.
Glasenberg served as CEO of Glencore from 2002 until his 2021 retirement.
After earning his MBA from the USC, Glasenberg started working as a marketer in the coal department of Marc Rich & Co. in his native South Africa.
The company became Glencore in 1994 and went public in 2011.
forbes_facts: Glasenberg is a former South African race-walking champion.
Glencore's founder Marc Rich, who fled the U.S. in 1983 after being indicted for multiple crimes including tax evasion, was pardoned by Bill Clinton in 2001.

name: Mikhail Prokhorov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2003-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Mikhail Prokhorov sold a 49% stake in the Brooklyn Nets to Alibaba executive Joseph Tsai in a $2.3 billion deal in 2018.
Much of Prokhorov's fortune stems from the 2008 sale of his stake in metals giant Norilsk Nickel.
He has stakes in Russian insurance and banking sectors.
He ran against Vladimir Putin in Russia's 2012 presidential race, gaining 8% of the vote.
He sold his last block of shares in UC Rusal one month before sanctions were imposed against the company by the US Treasury.
forbes_facts: The 6-foot-8 bachelor enjoys martial arts, skiing and windsurfing.
Prokhorov got Israeli citizenship in 2022.

name: Les Wexner
forbes_bio: Les Wexner founded L Brands, a global retail empire that included Victoria's Secret and Bath & Body Works, and served as CEO for more than 5 decades.
Wexner announced in 2020 that he would step down and sell a majority stake in Victoria's Secret for $525 million to a private equity firm.
Wexner got his start in 1963, when he used a $5,000 loan from his aunt to open The Limited, which sold only fast-moving items like shirts and pants.
His ex-confidant and financial manager Jeffrey Epstein was accused of sex trafficking. In 2019, Wexner said the late Epstein stole funds from him.
Wexner bought Victoria's Secret for $1 million in 1982, when it was just a small, failing chain of lingerie shops in San Francisco.
forbes_facts: Wexner collects Picasso paintings and vintage Ferraris, and has a 300-foot yacht, appropriately named Limitless.
Wexner has donated nearly a quarter of a billion dollars to institutions in Ohio, including Ohio State University's Wexner Medical Center.

name: Dirk Rossmann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: The eponymous company Dirk Rossmann founded at age 25 is now Germany's second-largest drugstore chain, with annual revenues of around $13 billion.
In 1972, he opened Germany's first self-service drugstore in Hannover just as price deregulation of pharmacy products was beginning.
Rossmann has made numerous private equity investments and owns a stake in the German Bundesliga soccer club Hannover 96.
He is a bestselling author. He published an autobiography in 2018, a novel, The Ninth Arm of the Octopus, in 2020, and its sequel, The Wrath of the Octopus, in 2021.
His German Foundation for World Population focuses on sex education and family planning, primarily in East Africa.

A proponent of sustainability, Rossmann in 2020 send the book We are the Weather to all members of the Bundestag and the boards of all Dax and M-Dax companies.

name: David Thomson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: David Thomson is one of six billionaire heirs to the media and publishing empire founded by his grandfather Roy Thomson (d. 1976).
The family's biggest holding: more than 310 million shares of Thomson Reuters, where Thomson serves as chairman.
Thomson owns around 14% of the business through the family's investment firm, Woodbridge.
The family's other assets include the Toronto-based Globe and Mail newspaper, and the Montreal Canadiens and Winnipeg Jets sports teams.

name: Hank Meijer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Hank Meijer owns Michigan-based grocery chain Meijer with his two brothers Doug and Mark.
Meijer has 500 stores in the Midwest and estimated revenues of $22 billion.
Hank and his brother served as co-CEOs from 1990 to 2017.
All three brothers are on Meijer's board. Hank is executive chairman.
His grandfather Henrik, a Dutch immigrant, started the company in 1934.
Hank's son Peter Meijer, one of 10 Republicans to vote to impeach Donald Trump, lost his primary to seek re-election to Congress in August 2022.
forbes_facts: Meijer pioneered the idea of one-stop shopping, now the staple of competitors like Walmart.
Over 700,00 people visit The Frederik Meijer Gardens & Sculpture Park in Grand Rapids, Michigan each year.

name: Rocco Commisso
forbes_bio: Rocco Commisso is the founder and CEO of cable company Mediacom, based in Chester, New York.
He previously worked as CFO at Cablevision Industries, which was acquired by Time Warner in 1995.
Commisso bought Italian Serie A soccer team Fiorentina in 2019 for a reported price of between $150 million and $200 million.
Commisso immigrated to America from Italy in 1962 at age 12. His first job was playing the accordion during movie theater intermissions.
He earned a full scholarship to Columbia University, which named its soccer stadium for him in 2013 in recognition of his donations to the school.
forbes_facts: Commisso was offered a tryout for the 1972 U.S. Olympic soccer team. He arrived out of shape and did not make the squad.
Commisso learned to play soccer in Italy on cement with a ball made out of old rags and underwear.

name: Anthony von Mandl
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Anthony von Mandl created the ready-to-drink alcoholic beverages White Claw Hard Seltzer and Mike's Hard Lemonade through his Mark Anthony Brands.
Forbes estimates von Mandl's U.S. business generated around $3.6 billion in revenue in 2025, based on analyst estimates.
He began his career in the Canadian wine business as an importer in the 1970s at age 22.
He currently owns six wineries in Canada, including Mission Hill Winery in British Columbia's Okanagan Valley.
forbes_facts: Von Mandl's spirits portfolio includes Ireland's top end Glendalough Whiskey & Gin Distillery.
In 2016, von Mandl was appointed as an Officer of the Order of Canada, the country's highest civilian honor.
Von Mandl got his start selling wine out of his car's trunk in Vancouver.

name: Richard White
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Richard White founded software company WiseTech Global in 1994 to help logistics companies manage goods and information across supply chains.
Since the company went public in 2016, WiseTech has been recording strong growth in revenue over the years, in part buoyed by acquisitions worldwide.
Touted as Australia's next Atlassian, Sydney-based WiseTech has more than 17,000 customers in 193 countries.
Its cloud-based logistics platform, CargoWise One, can automate dozens of steps.

In late 2024, White resigned from WiseTech, after 30 years as CEO, following reports of personal scandals. But from February 2025, he has assumed the title of executive chair and chief innovation officer, a role with an initial ten-year tenure.
forbes_facts: A former musician, refrigeration engineer and computer wholesaler, White has repaired guitars for top Australian rock bands like AC/DC and The Angels.
Before setting up WiseTech, White had started two other ventures in computer consulting and distribution of IT equipment.
In January 2026, WiseTech said it plans to buy the Canberra-based Centre for Customs and Excise Studies (CCES), a training provider in customs and border management.
